Subject: Aperture-XL-14B-v2 weights intake + validation / rollback planning

Team —

Aperture just pushed a new weights drop (Aperture-XL-14B-v2) and wants us to validate it for hosted + dedicated serving. They indicated significant token-efficiency improvements in their internal bench; see attached manifest + perf summary.

Primary asks from Product/Partnership:
- Quick compatibility assessment with our current runtime (quantization friendliness, KV cache layout, attention kernel changes).
- Safety/regression smoke tests (Hannah) and any known hallucination regression risks.
- Rollout/rollback plan and pinning recommendation: can we treat this as a drop-in upgrade or should we require a variant pin for 2 weeks?
- Resource delta estimate (GPUs, memory, quantized size) so infra can pre-allocate.

Timeline: Aperture would like a go/no-go within 48 hours if possible; otherwise they want to schedule a joint validation call.

Attachments: aperture-xl-14b-v2-manifest.json, perf-summary-apr-26.pdf, safety-eval-report.csv (from Aperture).

Action: please reply with the high-level compatibility blockers and whether you need a test VM with the raw weights (we can ask Aperture for S3 access). I’ll coordinate with Legal if we need an NDA amendment for the weights access.

— Laura
Laura Bennett
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Aperture-XL-14B-v2 weights intake + validation / rollback planning

On Sun, May 3, 2026 at 9:12 AM laura_bennett@redwood.ai wrote:
> Team —
> 
> Aperture just pushed a new weights drop (Aperture-XL-14B-v2) and wants us to validate it for hosted + dedicated serving.

Quick read: the manifest notes a mixed-precision export and a small architecture tweak (split rotary + rotary offset token handling). Two quick red flags for the runtime:

1) Quantization path: we currently rely on a per-layer symmetric INT8 path (compatible with most FP16->INT8 dumps). If Aperture's export uses per-channel calibration tables or newer quant formats (they mention "adaptive q8"), we'll need a short kernel path or a fallback to FP16/FP32 which impacts cost.

2) KV cache layout: the manifest indicates an altered KV concatenation order to support longer effective context. That will break cached session resumption unless we map their order to ours at load time; mapping is doable but non-trivial for live traffic.

I recommend:
- Get S3 read-only access to the weights and the export script (not just the manifest).
- Run our onboarding suite (INF-4829) on a staging node with both quantized and FP16 runs. Expect ~24–36 hours for a first pass.
- For rollouts: we should treat this as a separate variant (v2) and do canary routing (5/25/100) with automatic fallback rules if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds for tokens-per-request or if safety eval regresses.

I can start the bench-job today if Aperture can provide the tarball + checksums. Assigning ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4829

— Dev
Dev Patel 
Senior Systems Engineer — Serving Runtime
dev_patel@redwood.ai

Date: Sun, 03 May 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aperture-XL-14B-v2 weights intake + validation / rollback planning

Thanks — a few Product asks to help decisioning:

- Business gating: if perf claims hold, we want to include Aperture-XL-14B-v2 in our "curated" tier. That requires: parity on safety/regressions, <=5% latency regression for p50/p95 on typical 512-token chat loads, and deterministic rollback.
- Can we get an initial cost delta (tokens/$) estimate from infra so we can update pricing guidance?
- Rollout plan idea: canary at 5% (low-risk traffic e.g., internal apps) for 48 hours, then 25% for 24 hours, then full. Each step requires: (a) automated quality checks (Hannah), (b) observability flags green (Rohan), (c) legal/partner sign-off.

If timeline is tight we can do an "accelerated" path: dev runs perf and safety smoke in 24 hours; if green, we proceed to 5% canary.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Lead — Model Catalog
grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
From: rohan_mehta@redwood.ai

Date: Mon, 04 May 2026 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Aperture-XL-14B-v2 weights intake + validation / rollback planning

Quick infra notes:
- Need model size numbers (FP16 and q8) to size GPU pools and reserved VMs. If Aperture-XL-14B-v2 is ~26GB FP16 we can fit onto an A100-40; if the quantized path is 8–10GB we're fine on smaller SKUs.
- Canary routing: we should enable a configurable rollout window and an automated rollback trigger based on: 1) error rate >0.75%, 2) p95 latency > 2x baseline, 3) safety regression score delta > 0.02 (Hannah to define metric).
- If KV layout mapping is required (Dev's note), that may add ~6–10 hours of integration and require a short downtime window for warm caches unless we implement on-load remapping with existing keys.

I can pre-allocate a test GPU cluster (1 node) for the bench runs; confirm if we should use dedicated or hosted staging? If this is for a partner demo, dedicated staging is preferable.

— Rohan
Rohan Mehta
Principal Infra Engineer

Thanks for the quick loop. Attaching the S3 manifest and signed checksums here (see aperture-xl-14b-v2-manifest.json). We exported both per-channel-calibrated INT8 and a standard FP16 checkpoint; our adaptive q8 is optional — we included the calibration tables in the tarball.

Notes:
- We tested latency on a 40GB A100 and saw p95 improvements ~10% over v1 on conversational loads.
- The KV layout change was to support multi-turn context extension; we can provide a small shim that maps old->new ordering to help with backward compatibility. We'll upload the shim to the same S3 bucket.

S3 read-only link (expires in 7 days): https://s3.aperture.ai/redwood/intake/aperture-xl-14b-v2.tar.gz
Manifest checksum: sha256:5f2a9c...

If it helps, we can join a short call with Dev + Rohan to walk through the export and the shim.

— John
